patches.author: John Valentine
patches.comment:
Rustling leaves, with roar, vortex howl, and draughty whistle. Also distance and weather controls.

To use Draught Whistle, enable EQ Band 3 in FX. The Draught Whistle macro is only used at note-start, rather than dynamically during the note.

patches.author: John Valentine
patches.comment: Includes expression and playing styles: mute, sharp to soft plucking, playing over the hole or near the bridge, banjo, dual strings, and a reverb.

patches.comment: For keys, leads, or effects. Useful for occasional phrases to divert attention.

patches.name: FM EPiano Four High

1. Main sound with harmonics.
2. High 1:14
3. Main sound detuned.

patches.name: Pipe organ 2021
patches.author: John Valentine

Well temperament tuning from Jacky Ligon.
Demo: https://youtu.be/Rg_P84vODds

patches.name: Sweeping Distorted Pad
patches.author: John Valentine
patches.comment:
Six EQ sweeps over a complicated waveform, to highlight partials. Disable effect A1 or A2 to simplify.

A basic reverb is on Send FX 2 Level. Use the Ambient macro for slow movements.

Caution: when many sweep frequencies coincide, it might produce a sharp burst, so keep the conditioner (DYN) active. Reduce its sentivity with high polyphony.

patches.name: Claves (sticks)
patches.author: John Valentine
patches.comment:
Percussive wooden sticks with an attention-drawing sound. Useful for the offbeat, or for lead-in phrases before fresh music sections.

Plays well in the range C4-C7.

Source and resonator.

patches.name: Cymbal Tap

Hats through to gongs are possible.

patches.name: Handbells
patches.author: John Valentine
patches.comment:
Based on Databroth\Pads\Sweeping Bells

Has a wide range, but aliases above C8 (depending on your sample rate)

Try the 'Friction Sing' macro for singing bells or standing bowls.

patches.name: Noisy Synth Kick
patches.author: John Valentine
patches.comment:
Synthy kick drum with high-frequency hiss.
From the late 1980s.

Centered on note C5.

You can use this as basis for many parts of the drumkit.

Macros add noise, snare, distorted kicks, reverb tails.
Enable FX for more.

patches.name: Orchestral Bass Drum
patches.author: John Valentine
patches.comment: Tuned over a smaller range, for better pitch variation on keys. Play around C3.

patches.name: Taiko 2023
patches.author: John Valentine
patches.comment: Tuned over a smaller range, for better pitch variation on keys. Play around C3.

patches.name: Timpani
patches.author: John Valentine
patches.comment:
This patch can only produce two pitched of drum at a time. Set the Key Split to separate your two drum notes.

With thanks to Andreya [SST] for suggestion to use Split mode to solve the paraphonic problem.

patches.name: Tongue Drum 2022 Py12
patches.author: John Valentine
patches.comment:
- Comes with Py12 tuning. Switch off 'Tune' for ET12.
- Resonates in the range C4 to Eb5, but you can play any note.
- Resonance above 40% starts to intermodulate notes.
- Harmonics will cause higher resonances.
- Note length is how long your finger is on the drum. Quick taps give longer rings.
- If playing consistent arpeggios, set polyphony to arpeggio length, to help notes cancel on re-strike.

patches.name: Guitarp
patches.author: John Valentine
patches.comment: Macros 'Banjo' and 'Play at bridge' should not be used together.

patches.name: Solo Violin
patches.author: John Valentine
patches.comment:
Works in bass, cello, viola, and violin ranges.
You might want to enable MIDI settings > Controller Smoothing to reduce clicks from sudden controller changes.

patches.name: Cello 2021
patches.author: John Valentine
patches.comment: Works in bass, cello, viola, and violin ranges. Works best as a cello.

patches.name: Bassoon
patches.author: JV
patches.comment:
Plays well using Breath/Expression. Like the real instrument, you need to hit a (fairly wide) sweet spot.

To play the highest notes in the instrument's range, you need to increase 'Overblow', or set 'Higher modes' high and adjust your playing style.

With thanks to Andreya [SST] for technical troubleshooting. If you want bass notes to speak better, then enable all the modulations of 'Latest Key' and use Breath control to avoid the clicks on legato note changes.

patches.name: Cor Anglais
patches.author: JV
patches.comment: You might find this Cor Anglais is not easy to keep within its sweet spot. It can be unstable and inconsistent. Very high notes need pre-activating with a hard blow, or movement from a lower note. Try overblowing and other techniques.

patches.name: Flute
patches.author: JV
patches.comment:
If you don't want to use live velocity control:
1. Mute the Velocity modulations (attack speed, chiff amount).
2. Set AEG:Attack to zero.

patches.name: Oboe
patches.author: JV
patches.comment: Blow using the Breath macro/CC. At least 50% is needed to activate the reed. Thereafter, breath controls pipe resonance, and can be below 50% as long as resonance is maintained.
